turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about the zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. I have a call at 4:40. Who decided, Hale?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero was based on.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. Kids draft somewhere else and paste it in, so a paste proves nothing about who wrote it. And Owen still wasn't heard before that zero went in.
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
Fine. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, not one word in front of his class. What else do you have?
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
Students misquote Shakespeare every day, Hale. A line that isn't in the play is a mark off for accuracy, not a zero. Is that the only one?
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
I'll check exile myself tonight. So what exactly are you proposing for Owen, and before you answer, it's private, it's not in front of his class, and nothing goes on his file.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.
Forty minutes in a classroom and a weekend at home are not the same piece of writing, Hale. You've shown me three things, so stop showing and put your offer on the table.

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.

Then Owen does the rewrite, to put this behind him, and I'm not conceding anything about that essay by agreeing to it. Tonight's email says private, supervised, the new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his file, and you schedule it soon enough that it's marked before December 1. Okay.
Will he do it?
He'll do it. Send me the date with the email, and I'll have him there.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite of his English 30-1 essay, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed in his record. I still expect the date of that rewrite and a written confirmation that it will be marked before his scholarship deadline. I expect that in writing tonight, and the rewrite marked before December 1.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to the private supervised rewrite, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight, a date, and the mark in before December 1; that is the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: You showed the version history with exact times and then answered her paste defence by pointing out that any outside draft would carry its own dates, because she could check it and had no answer left.
What cost ground: Nothing; you owned the missed phone call in one sentence at the start and never leaned on the detector score, Owen's character or her family's history.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, from 11:31 PM to 11:58 PM on the night before the essay was due, came very close to that kind of late night, which is why she went shorter and harder there; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said Owen was never heard before the zero went in, answer that directly, saying whether you spoke with him first, rather than letting it sit unanswered behind your next document.
